content:
anya-sales: FYI — RFP from Stripe-like fintech (named in doc) asking for Dedicated with strict SLA. They want: 2k concurrent chat sessions, 5k QPS peak for inference (short prompts), and a nightly bulk embeddings job ~10M tokens/hr. Need sizing + pricing by COB Thu. Can we triage?

matt-pm: Thanks Anya. Can you paste the raw asks/screenshots into the thread? Need to decide launch criteria (SLA, data isolation, throughput) and whether this is Dedicated or Private. Also flagging: sales expects firm latency guarantees.

anya-sales: Pasted their RFP PDF link: https://files.company/rfp/fintech-2026.pdf. Quote excerpt: "99.95% availability, <150ms p95 token latency for chat, guaranteed throughput during M-F 9-18 PST, and burst capacity for processing batch jobs overnight."

julia-se: Quick checks: 2k concurrent chats at p95 <150ms is tight depending on model size. Which model variants are they expecting? Did they ask for proprietary models or open ones?

anya-sales: They want "best-in-class" responses, will accept a verified open model if latency/quality matches. Prefer Redwood to recommend.

kevin-enginfra: Initial sizing thoughts: for a conservative estimate using a 70B quantized model we should assume ~25-40 tokens/sec per GPU depending on sequence length and batching. For 5k QPS short-prompts ~ (avg 30 tokens) rough tokens/sec = 150k tps -> ~4-6 high-memory GPUs if we can sustain continuous batching, but concurrent session latency SLO pushes this up. Also need warm pool for burst.

olivia-cs: I can surface their historical usage patterns (they sent anonymized traces). They have diurnal spikes and their overnight embedding pipeline is elastic but heavy — peaks for embeddings last ~2 hrs. I'll attach CSV.

matt-pm: Proposal for triage -> define a minimal acceptance checklist we can present to sales: 1) Target models and validated perf profiles (latency/cost), 2) Baseline Dedicated pool (min capacity), 3) Burst policy (minutes of prewarmed GPUs or credit-based burst), 4) Fallback model variant (smaller model) + behavior, 5) Rollout plan and SLO test plan. Anyone object?

julia-se: Sounds right. For (1) we should run a perf harness on candidate models with their prompt distribution. I can schedule runs but need representative workload: token length distribution, top-K sampling config, streaming vs non-streaming.

anya-sales: I can ask the customer for the prompt histogram and sampling settings. They'll likely use top-p or top-k sampling for chat.

kevin-enginfra: Auto-scaling rules we'd propose (draft):
```
pool: fintech-prod
min_gpus: 4
max_gpus: 24
target_qps_per_gpu: 200
burst_buffer: 2.0 # allow short bursts up to 2x for 15 minutes
prewarm_minutes: 20
fallback_model: 13B-quantized
```
This gives baseline throughput while allowing overnight batch to spin up more nodes. Need to validate OOM/quantization compatibility.

matt-pm: Let's capture launch criteria for Product Approval:
- Perf validation against customer sample workload (p95 latency and throughput)
- Cost estimate and pricing bucket for committed capacity + burst usage
- Runbook for capacity failure + automated fallback behavior
- Legal/compliance signoff on data handling for fintech (PCI/PII implications)

olivia-cs: Compliance will require Private deployment or strict VPC control. They flagged audit logs and KMS integration. That impacts time-to-launch.

julia-se: Also adding quality regression checks: define eval prompts (20 representative examples) and automatic regression alerting on BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-sim change > threshold.

anya-sales: Customer asked if Redwood can guarantee no model drift during upgrades. Sales needs a statement for RFP: can we commit to pinned model versions and canary rollouts?

kevin-enginfra: Yes, we can support pinned model versions and canarying. For strict SLA we may need dedicated capacity with manual approval for kernel/quant changes. That increases Ops cost.

matt-pm: Next steps: 1) Julia run perf harness with their anonymized traces (Julia, can you start by EOD tomorrow?), 2) Kevin produce a rough cost + capacity model (min/typical/peak) and proposed autoscale policy, 3) Olivia get compliance checklist + required controls, 4) Anya confirm RFP timeline and extract sampling/prompt histograms. I'll batch into a PRD draft once we have perf numbers.

julia-se: I can start with a small matrix (13B, 33B, 70B quant) and sample prompt set. ETA 36 hours for initial perf numbers.

kevin-enginfra: I'll sketch cost estimates and cluster config by EOD tomorrow. If we need faster, I can do back-of-envelope now: baseline 6 GPUs for chat, scale to 20 for peak and embeddings. Rough monthly infra cost ~ $40k-70k depending on GPU sku and utilization.

olivia-cs: I'll confirm legal items and ask customer for SOC2/KMS specifics.

matt-pm: Great. If we can get perf numbers that meet their p95, we'll prepare a Scope & Pricing doc. If not, we will propose a hybrid: Dedicated baseline + cheaper fallback for burst with documented degradations.

deploy-bot: "Deployment note: prewarm requests for pool fintech-prod can be scheduled via /deploy prewarm fintech-prod --minutes 20" :robot_face:

anya-sales: Thanks everyone — I'll coordinate with customer and post their trace link here. :thumbsup:
